name: Acidic Soil
context: Essential for Oakleaf Hydrangeas, which thrive in the naturally acidic pine-heavy soils of the South.

name: Deciduous
definition: Plants that shed their leaves annually, usually in the autumn.
context: he American Beautyberry is deciduous, losing its leaves but keeping its bright purple berries into the winter.

name: Drought-Tolerant
definition: The ability of a plant to survive long periods without water.
context: Once established, Gulf Coast Muhly Grass and Spanish Bayonets are extremely drought-tolerant.

name: Evergreen
definition: A plant that retains green leaves throughout the year.
context: The Southern Magnolia is a classic broadleaf evergreen, providing greenery even in the middle of January.

name: Hardiness Zone
definition: A geographic area defined to encompass a certain range of climatic conditions relevant to plant growth and survival.
context: Most of the Souther United States falls into Zones 7-10.

name: Native Plant
definition: A plant that occurs naturally in a particular region without human intervention.
context: All five plants in your app are native to the Southern United States, making them better for local ecosystems.

name: Old Wood
definition: Stems that grew during the previous growing season.
context: Oakleaf Hydrangeas bloom on "old wood," meaning next year's flowers are already formed on the stems by late summer.

name: Ornamental Grass
definition: Grasses grown for their aesthetic appeal rather than for lawns or forage.
context: Gulf Coast Muhly Grass is one of the most popular ornamental grasses in the South.

name: Root Ball
definition: The main mass of roots at the base of a plant, including the surrounding soil.
context: When planting your Southern Magnolia, it is vital not to bury the root ball too deep, or the tree may suffocate.

name: Understory
definition: A layer of vegetation growing beneath the main canopy of a forest.
context: The American Beautyberry is an understory shrub, which is why it prefers the dappled light found under larger trees.
